name: Paraffin injection history

lead: Paraffin injection is a historic cosmetic filler practice. Hard and soft paraffin were injected to build up body contours, and the technique rose to a peak of popularity in the early 1900s. The intended appearance payoff was fuller contours, for example in the face, scalp or penile girth, without an operation.

The medical literature describes it mainly through complications: the body reacts to the injected mineral oil with a chronic foreign-body response called a paraffinoma or sclerosing lipogranuloma. Case series from Korea, Europe and elsewhere document lumps, ulcers, deformity and the need for excision and reconstruction.

paras: Historically, practitioners and sometimes people themselves injected paraffin, petrolatum or other mineral oils into the skin of the area to be enlarged. The wiki records the history for context and gives no technique. Modern fillers have replaced it in regulated cosmetic medicine.

Reported harms include painful swelling, ulceration, fistulae, deformity, skin necrosis, erectile and voiding problems after genital injection, and recurrence after excision. A forensic case report describes disseminated lipogranulomas and sudden death after self-injected mineral oil. Treatment is usually surgical.

chain: Paraffin is injected under the skin
It adds bulk in the injected area
The body forms a chronic reaction to the oil, which can distort the area
angle.text: People injected paraffin to add volume to a chosen area. The clinical record shows the volume effect coming with a foreign-body reaction that frequently deformed the tissue, which is why the practice is described historically.

lead: Paraffin injection refers to the historic use of liquid or semi-solid paraffin, and later mineral oil or petrolatum, injected under the skin to change body contours. A review of the field says injections of hard and soft paraffin to augment contour peaked in popularity in the early 1900s, after which their destructive consequences became widely recognised [1].

Its appeal as a way to look different was straightforward: a substance placed beneath the skin could add volume without an operation. The practice was used for contour changes such as penile enlargement and, per a case series, was also sold decades ago as a cure for baldness in the scalp [2][3].

Today the topic is documented almost entirely through clinical reports of paraffinoma, the granulomatous reaction to injected paraffin. A mini-review identified 124 penile cases between 1956 and 2017, with 80.6% involving liquid paraffin, most from Korea [4].

paras: Paraffin was first made as a wax in Germany in 1830 [5] and was used in medicine as injectable filler for body contour augmentation, a practice that a review places at its zenith in the early 1900s before the harm became widely recognised [1]. A case series of scalp paraffinomas describes patients treated 35 to 42 years earlier after responding to radio or newspaper advertisements that promised a cure for baldness [3].

Reports continued in the late 20th century, and a Korean review noted that such injections were still often performed by non-medical persons there [1]. Contemporary European reports describe an increase in penile paraffinoma cases presenting to hospitals [4].

Paraffinoma is a foreign-body granulomatous reaction. In the penile review, patients presented with pain or swelling, ulceration or fistulae, and deformity [4]. A case report of a man with self-injected mineral oil describes a 9 cm firm mass with phimosis, erectile dysfunction and voiding difficulty that resolved within weeks of surgery [2]. A Portuguese case describes a large ulcerated mass 30 years after injection [6]. Case reports also describe injection of petroleum jelly with ulceration of the genitalia [7]. A forensic report describes disseminated lipogranulomas and sudden death after self-administered mineral oil injection [8].
Paraffin reactions have also followed paraffin packing in nasal surgery, where authors note recurrences are frequent and mention potential carcinogenicity as a reason to attempt complete removal [9].

Most patients in the review needed surgical excision followed by reconstruction with split-skin grafts, scrotal skin flaps or preputial grafts [4]. A German series describes choosing between radical circumcision, mesh or full-thickness grafts and scrotal flaps depending on how far the paraffinoma extends [10]. A bilateral scrotal flap technique was reported in 1996 [11].

Evidence consists of case reports and case series rather than trials. A systematic search found 10 case series and 26 case reports covering 124 penile cases, with a mean age of 36.3 years and mean follow-up of 15.8 months [4]. A Korean review of 26 cases examined complications [1]. A study of sexual function and psychological characteristics in penile paraffinoma has also been published [12].

timeline.event: Paraffin wax is first produced by Carl Reichenbach in Germany [5].
Paraffin injection for contour augmentation reaches its peak popularity before its complications are widely recognised [1].
A review identifies 124 penile paraffinoma cases in the literature across this period [4].
A Korean review reports 26 penile cases and notes non-medical injections still occurring [1].
